title: QPoint: End-to-End Lightweight Point Cloud Processing via Robust Quaternion Feature Learning
claim: Our method reaches the highest accuracy at a fraction of the compute and parameters of competing approaches.
layout: 1 scatter plot, bubble size encodes parameters, dashed drop-lines to axes
description: A single scatter plot titled 'FLOPs vs Accuracy (Parameter Count as Circle Size)'. The x-axis is FLOPs in GFLOPs (0–14) and the y-axis is overall accuracy (92–95%). Six methods appear as distinct colored markers, each inside a translucent ellipse whose size encodes parameter count. Dashed colored lines drop from each marker to both axes. The red square for QPoint (Our) sits alone in the top-left corner, with the highest accuracy (about 94.7%), the lowest FLOPs (about 0.9G) and the smallest ellipse. Baselines (PointTransformer, Mamba3D, SIM, Point-M2AE) cluster around 3.5–5G with lower accuracy and larger ellipses. CloudTransformers lies far right at about 12.7G. A legend in the upper right lists the methods. The eye goes first to the isolated red marker in the corner.
caption: Accuracy-FLOPs-Parameter trade-off on ModelNet40.
abstract: The inherent sparsity, lack of structure, and rotation sensitivity of point clouds often lead to high computational and parameter cost in robust feature learning. To address these problems, we present QPoint, a lightweight framework that leverages robust quaternion feature learning. QPoint incorporates a Quaternion-Enhanced local perception module that uses learnable rotations to stabilize local features against geometric transformations, and a Quaternion global attention mechanism that employs quaternion similarity to capture global geometric context with inherent rotation invariance. Extensive experiments show that QPoint achieves top performance across multiple tasks. It achieves excellent 95.0%, 93.9%, and 92.1% on the challenging ScanObjectNN variants (OBJ BG, OBJ ONLY, PB T50 RS), 94.7% overall accuracy on ModelNet40, and 87.0% instance mIoU on ShapeNetParts. Furthermore, QPoint exhibits superior generalization in few-shot learning scenarios. Crucially, it accomplishes this with extremely minimal parameter and computational requirements, establishing a strong and efficient baseline for point cloud processing. Our source code is in the supplementary material and will be released to the public.
